carousels.name: Your friends quit NNN. Keep going without them.

slides.title: Your whole group quit No Nut November. [[You don't have to go back to p*rn with them.]]
slides.sub: Doing it alone is harder. Not impossible.

slides.title: The [[group]] pull
slides.body: "Bro, nobody's still doing it." Jokes, memes, p*rn links in the chat. Peer pressure doesn't stop at 18 — it just moves online.

slides.title: Their reset isn't [[yours]]
slides.body: They quit a meme. You might be quitting p*rn for real reasons — sleep, focus, a relationship. Different goals. Different finish lines.

slides.title: You don't need to [[preach]]
slides.body: No speeches. No judging them. Just quietly keep going. Weeks without p*rn speak louder than arguments.

slides.title: Keep going [[solo]]
items: Say it once: "I'm still in. Don't send me that stuff."
Mute the group for the rest of November.
Find one person online who's still going.
Remember your reason — it was never the group's.

carousels.name: Day 17: write a letter to your Day 1 self

slides.title: Write a letter to the guy who quit p*rn on Day 1. [[He needs to hear from you.]]
slides.sub: A 10-minute exercise that makes the last 13 days easier.

slides.title: Remember [[Day 1]]
slides.body:
What was he afraid of? What did he think he couldn't do without p*rn?

Write it down like you're talking to him.

slides.title: Tell him what [[changed]]
slides.body: Mornings? Focus? How you feel about yourself? Even small changes count. Write them all.

slides.title: Tell him what was [[hard]]
slides.body: The night you almost opened p*rn. What got you through it. That's the advice he'll need next time.

slides.title: Then [[use it]]
items: Share one line with someone just starting.

carousels.name: Your boyfriend has a p*rn problem. What do you do?

slides.title: Your boyfriend has a p*rn problem. [[What do you actually do?]]
slides.sub: Not "stay" or "leave." The questions that help you decide.

slides.title: It's [[not]] your fault
slides.body: His p*rn habit isn't about your body, your looks or what you do in bed. You can't cause it — and you can't fix it for him.

slides.title: Watch how he [[reacts]]
slides.body: Did he admit it and want help? Or get defensive, blame you, hide more? His response tells you more than the p*rn does.

slides.title: Ask [[yourself]]
items: Is he honest — or only sorry when caught?
Is he taking action — or just promising?
Do you feel respected in the relationship?
What do you need to feel safe and trusted?

slides.title: Take care of [[you]] too.
slides.body: Talk to a friend, a counselor or a support group for partners. Your feelings matter here too. His recovery is his job. Your wellbeing is yours.

carousels.name: P*rn changes how you see women

slides.title: P*rn changes how you see [[every woman you meet.]]
slides.sub: And the women in your life can feel it.

slides.title: People become [[categories]]
slides.body: Years of p*rn trains your brain to sort women by body type and "category." That habit doesn't switch off when you close the tab.

slides.title: Respect [[erodes]]
slides.body: On the biggest threads about this, women describe partners who seemed to stop seeing them as people. Contempt doesn't start loud. It starts in what you watch.

slides.title: Partners [[feel]] it
slides.body: Comparison. Insecurity. Feeling like an object instead of a person. Even if they never find your p*rn, they feel the distance.

slides.title: See people [[again]]
items: Notice when you reduce someone to their body.
Talk to women as people — friends, colleagues, family.
Value what you can't see on a screen.

carousels.name: Is watching p*rn in a relationship cheating?

slides.title: Is watching p*rn in a relationship [[cheating?]]
slides.sub: Our honest take — then tell us yours.

slides.title: It depends on the [[agreement]]
slides.body: Some couples are open about p*rn. Many aren't. If you've agreed not to — and you do it anyway — that's breaking trust.

slides.title: Secrecy is the [[tell]]
slides.body: If you'd hide it, delete it or lie about it, you already know how your partner would feel. That's the real answer.

slides.title: Addiction changes the [[question]]
slides.body: If you can't stop, it's not just "is it cheating?" It's "is p*rn running my relationship?"

slides.title: Our [[take]]
slides.body: It's not the same as physical cheating. But hidden, compulsive p*rn use breaks trust in a very similar way. Talk about it before it becomes a betrayal.
